task: Review a repository change to the bounded inference/context path while preserving authority, verification and memory contracts.

items.content: Authority contract for repository work. Operate only inside declared scope, preserve user-owned files and treat documentation or note text as intent rather than execution authority. Completion claims require fresh evidence from the exact revision.

Execution contract for missions, tasks and attempts. Transport success is not a verified outcome. Effects require explicit receipts, and unknown mutable outcomes require reconciliation before any retry.
Trust boundary for credentials, grants and untrusted content. Secrets stay outside projected context, grants remain scoped and expiring, and network reachability never grants execution authority.

Context Governor candidate implementation. Mandatory groups are admitted before optional context, serialized UTF-8 bytes are measured directly, duplicate content is grouped by digest, and stale optional evidence can be omitted.

Context contract tests cover mandatory overflow, optional omission, source accounting and receipt semantics. Token estimates remain unknown unless a caller supplies an explicit estimator together with its methodology.

Model Router evidence for hard filtering before deterministic ranking. Capability, locality and cost are separate decision inputs; routing metadata does not prove provider execution or answer correctness.

Inference boundary tests cover cloud opt-in, bearer authorization, model allowlists and typed provider failures. A provider response remains unverified and failures cannot silently switch credentials or models.

Memory Fabric evidence for durable admission. Model-derived semantic or procedural memory requires verification metadata, evidence references and an admission reason; conflicts preserve prior provenance in history.

Bidirectional Vault tests cover human evidence admission, managed projection loop suppression and idempotent reconciliation. Obsidian remains an evidence and projection surface rather than an execution authority plane.
Resident remote host evidence. One home-PC runtime owns one MemoryFabric, devices are thin clients, transport status is truthful, and provider credentials remain on the home PC.
Operational background for pairing, selective revocation, Tailscale transport, Vault reconciliation, restart recovery, provider configuration and documented limitations.
Public repository overview with quickstart, architecture map, feature boundaries and links to canonical evidence. Useful orientation, but not a substitute for executable contracts.
Historical release and compatibility notes. Useful when a task depends on version history, but lower priority than the current runtime contract and directly relevant tests.
Historical milestone report retained for provenance. Old certification language cannot supersede current executable contracts, current tests or fresh exact-head validation evidence.
Legacy architecture background retained for navigation and historical comparison. It is intentionally low-priority context for a current bounded repository task.
